info.name: 48Date Backend API
info.description:
# 48Date Backend API

REST API for the 48Date dating app backend (NestJS + Prisma + PostgreSQL).

## Base URL

Use the collection variable `baseUrl` (default `http://localhost:3000`).

## Unified response envelope

**Every** endpoint returns the same shape:

### Success

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Account created successfully",
  "messages": [],
  "data": { }
}
```

- `success` — always `true` for 2xx responses
- `message` — one short, human-readable summary (non-technical)
- `messages` — array of extra messages (usually empty on success)
- `data` — the actual payload (user, tokens, profile, ...)

### Error

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "Validation failed",
  "messages": ["phone must be a valid international number", "password must be at least 8 characters"],
  "statusCode": 400
}
```

- `success` — always `false`
- `message` — one short, human-readable summary
- `messages` — every individual message (each validation failure, etc.)
- `statusCode` — the HTTP status code

## Formatted user response

Anywhere a user profile is returned (Register, Login, Google Login, Verify OTP, Me, Profile, Discovery), `data.user` (or `data`) is **categorized** so clients can render sections directly:

| Section | Contents |
|---|---|
| `auth` | phone, email, role, `isEmailVerified`, `isPhoneVerified`, `isUserVerified` |
| `basicProfile` | name, firstName, lastName, username, birthDate, occupation, gender, interestedIn |
| `lifestyle` | smoker, alcohol, kids, wantsKids, lookingFor |
| `location` | locations (array), lastLocation, latitude, longitude |
| `body` | heightCm, weightKg |
| `interests` | creativity[], sports[], moviesAndDramas[] |
| `media` | images[], selfieUrl, selfieVerified, notificationsEnabled |
| `meta` | subscriptionId, lastLoginAt, createdAt, updatedAt |

`passwordHash` is never included in any response.

## Authentication

- **Access token** — short-lived (15 min), carries `{ sub: userId, role }`. Required for protected endpoints via `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`.
- **Refresh token** — long-lived (7 days), used only at `POST /auth/refresh` to get a new token pair.
- **OTP / verification endpoints are PUBLIC** — `request-otp`, `verify-otp`, `forgot-password`, `verify-forgot-password`, `reset-password` take phone/email + channel directly and do **not** require a Bearer token.

The collection auto-saves `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, and `resetToken` from responses via test scripts — run Register/Login first and the protected requests just work.

## Request serials & Domain Folders

Every request carries a stable serial ID: `<Folder>-<NN>`.

| Folder | Prefix | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Auth** | `A-NN` | Registration, login, OTP verification, password recovery, refresh, profile me |
| **Users** | `B-NN` | Profile setup & updates, complete profile fetching |
| **Images** | `C-NN` | Multipart photo uploads to Cloudflare R2 / local disk |
| **Discovery** | `D-NN` | Candidate browsing, preference filters, swiping (LIKE/PASS/SUPER_LIKE) |
| **Matches** | `E-NN` | Active mutual matches list and unmatching |
| **Chat** | `F-NN` | Conversation rooms, paginated message histories (+ WebSockets Gateway) |
| **Games** | `G-NN` | In-chat mini-games, answer submissions, compatibility calculation |
| **Dates** | `H-NN` | Mapbox place search, date proposals, user dates list, ratings & status updates |
| **Blocks** | `I-NN` | User blocking, list blocked users, unblock user |
| **Reports** | `J-NN` | Submit moderation report, list filed reports |
| **Subscriptions** | `K-NN` | Subscription plans, current user subscription status, RevenueCat webhook |
| **Trust Score** | `L-NN` | User trust score & badges, trust history timeline |
| **Success Stories** | `M-NN` | Submit success story, feed, story detail, toggle like, comments |

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Authentication endpoints: register → verify OTP → login → refresh → password reset → logout (or Google login).

**Suggested flow to try the whole collection (serials in parentheses):**
1. `A-01 Register` (or `A-11 Google Login`, auto-saves tokens)
2. `A-03 Request OTP` (returns the dummy code `123456`)
3. `A-04 Verify OTP` (marks the channel verified)
4. `A-02 Login` (auto-saves a fresh token pair)
5. `A-10 Me` (see the categorized profile)
6. `A-08 Refresh` (rotate the refresh token)
7. `A-09 Logout`
8. `A-05 Forgot Password` → `A-06 Verify Forgot Password` → `A-07 Reset Password`

Every response uses the unified envelope: `{ success, message, messages, data }` on success, `{ success: false, message, messages, statusCode }` on error.

User profiles in responses are grouped into sections: `auth`, `basicProfile`, `lifestyle`, `location`, `body`, `interests`, `media`, `meta`.

request.description:
Creates a new user account. Only phone or email and password are required. Additional profile fields can optionally be provided during registration. Returns the categorized profile (no password hash) plus a JWT access/refresh token pair inside the envelope's `data`.

### Request Body — raw JSON (Minimal)

```json
{
  "phone": "+8801700000000",
  "email": "test@48date.com",
  "password": "password123"
}
```

### Field Reference

- **Required**:
  - `password` (string, min 8 characters)
  - At least one of `phone` (E.164 format, e.g. `+8801700000000`) or `email` (valid email address)
- **Optional Basic Profile**:
  - `name`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `username`, `occupation` (strings)
  - `birthDate` (ISO 8601 date string in the past)
  - `gender` (`MALE`, `FEMALE`, `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY`)
  - `interestedIn` (`MALE`, `FEMALE`, `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY`)
- **Optional Lifestyle**:
  - `smoker` (`REGULAR`, `OCCASIONALLY`, `NONE`)
  - `alcohol` (`REGULAR`, `OCCASIONALLY`, `NONE`)
  - `kids` (`HAVE`, `DONT_HAVE`)
  - `wantsKids` (boolean)
  - `lookingFor` (`REAL_RELATIONSHIP`, `SOMETHING_MEANINGFUL`, `SEE_WHERE_IT_GOES`, `NEW_FRIENDS_FIRST`)
- **Optional Location & Body**:
  - `locations` (string array), `lastLocation` (string)
  - `heightCm` (integer, 50–250), `weightKg` (integer, 20–300)
- **Optional Interests**:
  - `creativity` (subset of: `Art`, `Design`, `Makeup`, `Photography`, `Singing`)
  - `sports` (subset of: `Running`, `Gym`, `Soccer`, `Cricket`, `Tennis`, `Basketball`)
  - `moviesAndDramas` (subset of: `TV Shows`, `Romance`, `Comedy`, `K-Drama`, `Horror`, `Thriller`, `Sci-Fi`, `Fantasy`, `Anime`, `Zombie`)
- **Optional Media**:
  - `images` (array of 1–6 objects: `{ url: string, isMain: boolean, sortOrder?: number }`, exactly one `isMain: true`)
  - `selfieUrl` (valid URL string)
  - `notificationsEnabled` (boolean)

request.description:
Logs in with phone or email + password. On success returns the categorized profile, a fresh token pair (inside `data`), and updates the user's `lastLoginAt`.

### Request Body — raw JSON (Phone)

```json
{
  "phone": "+8801700000000", // E.164 format
  "password": "password123"
}
```

### Request Body — raw JSON (Email)

```json
{
  "email": "test@48date.com",
  "password": "password123"
}
```

> Send as **raw JSON** with `Content-Type: application/json`.

### Notes

- Provide either `phone` or `email` along with `password`.
- Wrong phone/email or wrong password returns `401` with `message: "Invalid credentials"` (no account enumeration).
- This request auto-saves a fresh `accessToken` / `refreshToken` into collection variables.

response.name: Success — 200 OK
Error — 401 Invalid credentials
Error — 400 Validation

request.description:
Requests a verification code for an account. **Public endpoint — no Bearer token required.** Identifies the account by the phone or email that matches the chosen channel. **Dummy implementation:** no message is sent; the fixed code `123456` is returned inside `data` for development.

### Request Body — raw JSON

```json
{
  "channel": "phone",              // REQUIRED — which channel to verify: "email" or "phone".
  "phone": "+8801700000000"        // REQUIRED when channel is "phone" — E.164 format.
  // "email": "test@48date.com"    // REQUIRED instead when channel is "email".
}
```

### Notes

- Provide **exactly one** identifier matching the channel: `phone` with `channel: "phone"`, or `email` with `channel: "email"`. Mismatches return `400`.
- The endpoint deliberately does not check whether the account exists (no account enumeration) — `verify-otp` will return `404` for unknown identifiers.
- When Twilio Verify / SMTP are integrated, this endpoint will actually send the code and stop returning it.

response.name: Success — 201 Created
Error — 400 Channel/identifier mismatch

request.description:
Verifies the OTP for an account and flips the matching verification flag. **Public endpoint — no Bearer token required.** Generates and returns access & refresh tokens on success.

- `channel: "phone"` + valid OTP → `isPhoneVerified: true`
- `channel: "email"` + valid OTP → `isEmailVerified: true`
- Both cases keep `isUserVerified: false` until profile setup is complete.

### Request Body — raw JSON

```json
{
  "channel": "phone",              // REQUIRED — "email" or "phone".
  "phone": "+8801700000000",       // REQUIRED when channel is "phone".
  "otp": "123456"                  // REQUIRED — exactly 6 digits (dummy is 123456).
}
```

response.name: Success — 201 Created
Error — 401 Invalid OTP
Error — 404 No account found
Error — 400 Validation

request.description:
Requests a password-reset OTP for an account. **Public endpoint — no Bearer token required.** Identifies the account by phone or email matching the chosen channel. **Dummy implementation:** returns the fixed code `123456`; no message is sent.

### Request Body — raw JSON

```json
{
  "channel": "email",              // REQUIRED — which channel to send the reset code through: "email" or "phone".
  "email": "test@48date.com"       // REQUIRED when channel is "email".
  // "phone": "+8801700000000"     // REQUIRED instead when channel is "phone".
}
```

### Notes

- Same channel/identifier rules as `request-otp`: provide exactly one identifier matching the channel, else `400`.
- The endpoint does not reveal whether the account exists (no account enumeration) — the next step (`verify-forgot-password`) returns `404` for unknown identifiers.
- Next step: send the OTP to `verify-forgot-password` to get a `resetToken`.

response.name: Success — 201 Created
Error — 400 Validation

request.description:
Verifies the password-reset OTP and issues a **short-lived reset token** (15 minutes) used by `reset-password`. **Public endpoint — no Bearer token required.**

### Request Body — raw JSON

```json
{
  "channel": "phone",              // REQUIRED — the channel you requested the reset code through.
  "phone": "+8801700000000",       // REQUIRED when channel is "phone".
  // "email": "test@48date.com",   // REQUIRED instead when channel is "email".
  "otp": "123456"                  // REQUIRED — exactly 6 digits. The dummy code is always 123456.
}
```

### Notes

- Wrong OTP → `401 Invalid OTP`; unknown identifier → `404`.
- The response auto-saves `resetToken` into the collection variable (see the *Tests* tab) — `reset-password` is pre-filled with `{{resetToken}}`.
- The token expires after 15 minutes; expired tokens return `401` at `reset-password`.

response.name: Success — 201 Created
Error — 401 Invalid OTP

request.description:
Sets a new password using the reset token from `verify-forgot-password`. **Public endpoint — no Bearer token required.**

### Request Body — raw JSON

```json
{
  "resetToken": "{{resetToken}}", // REQUIRED — from verify-forgot-password. Pre-filled via collection variable.
  "newPassword": "newpassword456"  // REQUIRED — minimum 8 characters.
}
```

### Notes

- Invalid or expired reset token → `401 Invalid or expired reset token`.
- After a successful reset, log in with the new password.

response.name: Success — 201 Created
Error — 401 Invalid or expired reset token
Error — 400 Validation

request.description:
Exchanges a valid refresh token for a new access/refresh token pair. Use this when the access token expires (after 15 minutes).

### Request Body — raw JSON

```json
{
  "refreshToken": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs..." // REQUIRED — the refresh token from Register/Login. Uses {{refreshToken}} if left empty.
}
```

> The request is pre-filled with the collection variable `{{refreshToken}}` (auto-saved by Register/Login).

### Notes

- Expired or invalid refresh tokens return `401`.
- The response auto-saves the new token pair, so the protected requests keep working.

response.name: Success — 200 OK
Error — 401 Invalid or expired refresh token

request.description:
Logs the user out. Requires a valid Bearer token (the endpoint confirms it), after which the client should **discard its stored tokens**.

### Headers

- `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` — required (auto-filled from Register/Login).

### Body

- None. Do not attach a body.

### Notes

- Logout is stateless for now (JWT tokens can't be revoked server-side without extra infrastructure). A Redis blacklist can be added later to make it server-enforced.

response.name: Success — 201 Created
Error — 401 Missing/invalid token

request.description:
Returns the authenticated user's full profile inside `data`, **categorized** into sections (`auth`, `basicProfile`, `lifestyle`, `location`, `body`, `interests`, `media`, `meta`), including uploaded images (ordered by `sortOrder`).

### Headers

- `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` — required (auto-filled from Register/Login).

### Body

- None. This is a GET request — do not attach a body.

### Notes

- The response never includes `passwordHash`.
- `media.images` is an array of the user's photo records; empty until photos are added.

item.name: Date Planner
item.description:
Date planning endpoints for coordinating, accepting, updating, cancelling, and completing in-person dates.

### Date Flow:
1. Search venue (`G-01`)
2. Propose a date (`G-02`) — posts a `DATE_INVITE` message to chat
3. Counterpart accepts (`G-06`) or declines (`G-07`)
4. Reschedule/update if needed (`G-05`)
5. Either participant can cancel (`G-08`)
6. Mark complete after date happens (`G-09`)
7. List / view date plans (`G-03`, `G-04`)
